claims_rejected.why: illustrated, not stated: the king dies on seeing and hearing her (கண்டளவே தோற்றான் ... உண்டளவே தோற்றான் உயிர்); no one states a rule

claims.gist: consciousness arises from the combined elements as intoxication arises from mixed தாதகிப் பூ and jaggery
consciousness perishes when the elements separate, as the sound of a drum dies
perception alone is a means of knowledge; inference (கருத்து அளவு) fails
this life and its fruit are all; a next world where deeds are reaped is false

claims_rejected.why: classification of conscious and non-conscious elements is part of the same doctrine, folded into the claims at 264-267

units.note: Stance taken as refuted because Manimekalai answers the materialist at 284-287, just outside this unit.

claims.gist: the whole world is an egg laid by one god (the Brahmavadi)
Narayana is the world's protector, from the purana of the sea-coloured one
the Veda with its six limbs is uncaused, without beginning or end, and is the path

claims_rejected.why: Manimekalai's verdict that these views fit no valid means of knowledge is a judgment on the speakers, not a doctrine of its own

units.note: The refutation is the brief verdict at 106-107 (இசையாது இவர் உரை).

claims_rejected.why: narrated, not stated: Neelakesi's conversion after taking the great one's dharma is told as event, with no general claim drawn

claims.gist: dharma becomes death (அறங்கூற்றம்) to those who do wrong, as the learned say, and the saying is not false

claims_rejected.why: the queen's death as the fruit of the king's deed is shown, not stated as a rule

units.note: The saying is set off with என்னும் ... சொல், but it matches no Kural or Naladiyar wording, so no echo.

claims.gist: one knows even one's parents only by inference, so denying inference fails
without true understanding the true nature of things is hard to know; the materialist is left with doubt

claims_rejected.why: narrative close: she learned the five schools; not a claim

units.note: School taken from the speaker, Manimekalai, as the Buddhist inquirer answering the Lokayata.

claims.gist: atoms are beginningless, indestructible, are not newly produced, do not enter one another or change kind
atoms do not split or flatten but move, sink and rise, combine into mountains and other bodies, and separate back into their own nature
when atoms form an element they combine in unequal or equal proportions (one, three-quarter, half, quarter) and the element is named by the predominant atom
earth is hard and sinks, water is cool and tasted and flows down, fire burns and rises, wind moves sideways and stirs

claims_rejected.why: விபரீதத்தால் வேற்று இயல்பு எய்தும் is too compressed to state separately; folded into the elemental qualities

units.note: Assigned to the Ajivika speaker introduced at 108; the answer comes only at 166, so reported here.

claims.gist: killing a thief is not tyranny but the victory of the king's spear (just punishment)
for women who have lost their husbands there is nothing left to show (no recourse)

claims_rejected.why: the king's self-condemnation (யானோ அரசன் யானே கள்வன்) is a confession about himself, not a general claim, though it overturns line 74 in act

units.note: Line 74 is the king's view, reversed by the scene but not answered as doctrine, so reported.

claims.gist: the Lord is free of birth and the other three (பிறப்பு ஆதி நான்கு இல்லான்)
his word removes the sufferings of beings and gives them highest bliss
the one who knows all things (எல்லாம் உணர்ந்தான்) alone is to be praised as God

claims_rejected.why: தருமச் சுடரான் is an epithet, not a separate claim

claims.gist: gain, loss, obstacle, arrival, pleasure, pain, birth and death are all fixed at conception
pleasure and pain too are atoms
prior destiny (முன் உள ஊழ்) alone brings about what follows

claims_rejected.why: the question put to the Nigantha is a request, not a claim

units.note: Stance refuted on the strength of சொல் தடுமாற்றத் தொடர்ச்சியை விட்டு (166), a dismissal rather than an argument.

claims.gist: Purusha is not of the three gunas, is single, all-pervading, eternal, pure consciousness that knows all things
there are twenty-five principles: five elements, five sense organs, five sense objects, five organs of action, mind, intellect, ego, citta, and the soul

claims_rejected.why: செயிர் அறச் செப்பிய is praise of the exposition, not endorsement of the doctrine
modesty topos: even the white moon is not spotless, so my words are not all virtue; an authorial apology, not a doctrinal or ethical claim

claims.gist: there are eight fallacies of knowledge (பிரமாண ஆபாசம்): bare indication, error, doubt, unexamined certainty, non-cognition, the non-existent, re-cognition, and recollection
the schools Lokayata, Buddhist, Sankhya, Nyaya, Vaisheshika and Mimamsa, with teachers Brihaspati, Jina, Kapila, Akshapada, Kanada and Jaimini, each fix their means of knowledge
the means of knowledge now in use are perception, inference, testimony, comparison, presumption and non-existence

claims_rejected.why: examples (shell taken for silver, post or man) illustrate the fallacies and are not separate claims

units.note: Sinon (சினன்) as the Buddhist teacher is the speaker's attribution; claims tagged vedic as the pramana-teacher's account.
